theme.title: Quiet Session
theme.summary: Materials (+0.15%) and Real Estate (+0.09%) led the market today, while Consumer Discretionary (-0.39%) and Industrials (-0.18%) brought up the rear. Performance didn't cluster cleanly by style — growth averaged -0.10%, defensives -0.03%, and value/cyclicals -0.03% — more a stock-by-stock market than a single broad theme. That shows up at the index level too: the blue-chip Dow gained +0.26% while the tech-heavy Nasdaq fell -0.76%, a wide enough gap to matter. Small caps underperformed as well, with the Russell 2000 at -0.76%, hinting the move favored large, established balance sheets over smaller, more rate-sensitive companies. The VIX fell 0.32% to 15.79, which reads as an orderly rotation rather than panic-driven selling. Gold added 0.05% to $4,690.60, crude oil was little changed at $82.43, and bitcoin slipped 0.07% — cross-asset moves weren't all pointing the same direction as equities.
